_comment: One profile matrix for every platform. The launchers (bash on Linux/macOS,
PowerShell on Windows) both read this file; nobody hard-codes switches.
Selection: the first profile whose match.os and match.vendor apply, with
optional vram_min_mb / vram_max_mb bounds. Later profiles are fallbacks.
Every number here was measured or taken from a test report; see docs/FORK.md,
and do not add a value that has not been measured on that platform.

profiles.name: linux-amd-16gb
profiles.note: RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.3.1. 512 MB card buffers: median 0.60-0.70 fps, 10th percentile 0.30-0.40 vs 0.10 at 1024 (two sweeps, 0 removals) - the steadiest configuration measured. Do not raise LATE_WAIT: 3 removes the device. Texture budget 4096 MB: texture phase 350 -> 40-48 ms, frame 1,464-1,976 -> 1,046-1,182 ms, median 0.80-1.00 (two runs, no removals). Section views on by default under Wine (code, not a variable): one mapping per section, view unmaps 44,000 -> 0, frame 1,203-1,448 -> 750-952 ms, median 0.80 -> 1.10-1.30 across three runs each. Indirect window + runs on (from #8/#9, AST/steve ports of fxceless): two quick runs each 3.95 fps / 255-259 ms against 3.05-3.25 default, p10 3.30, no removals. VICTORY_INDIRECT_WINDOW=0 or RUNS=0 if a long session ever loses the device. Card hash lanes on (from #11, astrosteveo): GPU phase 88-110 -> 31.7 ms, frame 226 -> 150 ms, median 4.45 -> 6.60/6.70 across two runs, no removals; NVIDIA measured 5.25-5.30 vs 4.40-4.65 by the author. VICTORY_CARD_HASH_LANES=0 turns it off. 1024 MB card buffers measured again on the current save's scene: 4.70/4.70 fps at 512 vs 5.50/5.60 at 1024 (four runs interleaved, p10 2.6-3.0 vs 2.5-3.4, 0 removals); the old 512 note was the opening scene before a save moved it.

profiles.name: linux-nvidia-16gb
profiles.note: RTX 5080 16 GB, NVIDIA 620.73.04, Proton Experimental 11.0-20261112, the wineserver from tools/build-wineserver.sh, main at 6f3375d. Nine runs in turn: 4.30 / 4.30 / 4.30 fps with the linux-nvidia values, 5.20 / 5.20 / 5.20 with VICTORY_INDIRECT_RUNS=1 too, 6.20 / 5.85 / 5.75 with VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 as well; frame at 3,000 draws 226 -> 189 -> 169 ms; no removals, and none in a 20-minute run of this profile (6.30 fps) or in a run with Proton's own wineserver. LATE_WAIT 3 removes the device on AMD under Linux: set VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=1 first if a session here loses it. Not measured: NVIDIA cards under 16 GB (they keep linux-nvidia), other driver versions, play beyond the first scene after the opening. The relay with a copy queue of its own, the copy-back through the layer's own view and lazy tracking of title writes (VICTORY_RELAY=2, VICTORY_RELAY_QUEUE=1, VICTORY_BACK_OWN_VIEW=1, VICTORY_ALIAS_LAZY=1; docs/FINDINGS.md 2.12, 2.14, 2.18 and 2.20), 200 s runs in turn at 5aa7b69: 5.10 / 5.40 / 5.35 fps without them and 6.00 / 5.90 / 5.70 with the relay and its queue; in a later set 6.00 / 5.40 / 5.80 with those two and 6.20 / 6.40 / 6.50 with all four; frame at 3,000 draws 175 -> 157 -> 148 ms. No removals in 33 runs of 200 s with the relay and its queue, nor in two 20-minute runs with all four (7.10 fps at 3840x2160 output, 9.70 fps with VICTORY_OUTPUT=2560x1440). Set VICTORY_RELAY=0 first, then VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=1, if a session here loses the device. Not measured with these four: AMD (the relay is not safe under RADV), Windows, NVIDIA cards under 16 GB. Every title buffer's copy in the card's memory (VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_KB=64, VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=2048; docs/FINDINGS.md 2.23): atomics on small buffers no longer cross the bus; 200 s runs in turn at 2560x1440 output, medians by 200 draws or more: 8.80 / 9.20 / 9.40 fps before, 10.80 / 11.20 / 10.80 with it; no removals. With the list that sends changes up grouped as well (VICTORY_SYNC_GROUPED=1; docs/FINDINGS.md 2.24), at main f5c728c: 11.00 / 11.60 / 10.90 fps without it, 11.90 / 11.60 / 11.70 with it; no removals. With fills of upload memory that do not wait for submissions sent ahead as well (VICTORY_FILL_AHEAD=1; docs/FINDINGS.md 2.26), on the code of 2.25: 12.80 / 12.40 / 12.30 fps without it, 12.90 / 13.40 / 13.10 with it; no removals, and its check found no fill that read bytes a submission then changed. If the log says that fills wait again, the check found one: report the line. With the stores of the title's culling programs bounded as well (VICTORY_CULL_RANGES=1; docs/FINDINGS.md 2.27), at main 1b905d4 with the change: 13.50 / 13.75 / 13.40 fps without it, 13.90 / 14.20 / 14.65 with it, and 13.70 against 14.65 over ten more rounds of 110 s runs; no removals; a diagnostics build with VICTORY_CULL_RANGES=check found no byte stored outside a bound in the opening and the first scene of the world. Not measured: later scenes. Unset it first if objects go missing or flicker in a later scene, and report it.

profiles.name: linux-other
profiles.note: Intel/other Vulkan drivers: mesh shaders and SM 6.6 required. Report results, then promote to a measured profile.

profiles.name: windows-amd
profiles.note: README combo. If the Adrenalin DXIL compiler crashes (amdxc64.dll), add VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=59 (issue #422) and the RDNA4 skips from issue #3.

profiles.name: windows-nvidia
profiles.note: Windows + NVIDIA. Ported from the measured linux-nvidia-16gb set (INDIRECT_RUNS 4.30 -> 5.20 fps, CARD_HASH_LANES 4.40 -> 5.25, both RTX 5080; TEXTURE_NO_WAIT from every measured NVIDIA profile) and the Windows set from trustno1-coder/VIctory-NVIDIA. The title's own 30 fps cap is lifted to 60 (VICTORY_FRAME_INTERVAL_MS=16.667); it only shows where the card renders faster than 33 ms. Not yet measured on Windows: report the fps and any device removal. If a session loses the device, set VICTORY_RELAY=0, then VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=1. A first Windows run is in docs/FORK.md (RTX 4090, main @ 47d9a33: 7.20-8.20 fps, no device removed, picture correct); one run only, so still reported.

profiles.name: windows-other
profiles.note: Requires a D3D12 GPU with SM 6.6 and mesh shaders.

overrides.name: safe
overrides.note: No submissions ahead of the fence. Slowest, most stable. Use it when a run dies with 'device removed'.

overrides.name: diagnostics
overrides.note: Verbose GPU logging for bug reports.
